+name: android-ndk-preinstall
+description: >-
+  Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK so Gradle configuration never
+  triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download mid-build. gh-1655: one
+  truncated android-ndk-r28c-linux download ("Error on ZipFile unknown
+  archive" at 33%) red'd the ci.yml build-android leg — and the aggregate
+  Quality gate with it — because AGP's in-configuration auto-install path
+  has NO retry. The NDK version is resolved from the pinned Flutter SDK's
+  own gradle plugin source (the exact value flutter.ndkVersion resolves
+  to — no second pin to drift), the install is skipped when the NDK is
+  already present, and the download itself is bounded-retried — the same
+  hardening the flutter_gemma Android seed carries (gh-1468). Companion
+  guard: test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart.
+runs:
+  using: composite
+  steps:
+    - name: Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK (bounded retry)
+      shell: bash
+      run: |
+        set -euo pipefail
+        # flutter.ndkVersion's single source of truth: the gradle plugin
+        # bundled with the SDK flutter-action installed. app/
+        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so
+        # resolving here can never skew from what AGP requests at
+        # configuration time (a literal pin on either side would break
+        # that coupling — the guard test pins both sides).
+        if [ -n "${FLUTTER_ROOT:-}" ]; then
+          FLUTTER_HOME="$FLUTTER_ROOT"
+        else
+          FLUTTER_BIN="$(command -v flutter || true)"
+          if [ -z "$FLUTTER_BIN" ]; then
+            echo "::error::cannot locate flutter (set FLUTTER_ROOT) — the NDK pre-install resolves the version from the SDK's gradle plugin source"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          FLUTTER_HOME="$(dirname "$(dirname "$FLUTTER_BIN")")"
+        fi
+        GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_HOME/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"
+        NDK_VERSION="$(grep -hoE 'val ndkVersion: String = "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"' "$GRADLE_SRC" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)"
+        if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
+          echo "::error::cannot resolve flutter.ndkVersion from $GRADLE_SRC — the Flutter gradle plugin layout moved; update the extraction in .github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall (and test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart) TOGETHER"
+          exit 1
+        fi
+        echo "resolved flutter.ndkVersion = $NDK_VERSION"
+        ANDROID_SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-/usr/local/lib/android/sdk}"
+        SDKMANAGER="$ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
+        if [ ! -x "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
+          SDKMANAGER="$(command -v sdkmanager || true)"
+        fi
+        if [ -z "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
+          echo "::error::sdkmanager not found (expected $ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager) — the NDK pre-install needs the Android cmdline-tools"
+          exit 1
+        fi
+        # Idempotence: AGP resolves `ndkVersion` against
+        # $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/<version> — source.properties present means
+        # the NDK is fully installed; skip the download entirely.
+        if [ -f "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties" ]; then
+          echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION already installed — skipping pre-install"
+          exit 0
+        fi
+        # Accept any license the image has not pre-accepted so the
+        # installs below never prompt (|| true: `yes` dies of SIGPIPE by
+        # design once sdkmanager stops reading).
+        yes | "$SDKMANAGER" --licenses > /dev/null || true
+        # gh-1655: Gradle's own auto-install (the same sdkmanager call,
+        # run inside configuration) has no retry — one truncated download
+        # unzips as "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" and the build dies.
+        # Here the same download gets three attempts with backoff.
+        for attempt in 1 2 3; do

+          rm -rf "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION"
+          if "$SDKMANAGER" --install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION"; then
+            echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION installed"
+            exit 0
+          fi
+          echo "::warning::sdkmanager NDK install failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
+          sleep 10
+        done
+        echo "::error::NDK $NDK_VERSION install failed after 3 attempts — gh-1655 red'd the leg on a single truncated archive; inspect the sdkmanager output above"
+        exit 1

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1656
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1656
- **Title**: gh-1655 [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1655` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +726
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-16T14:03:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T11:24:06Z

## PR Description

Closes #1655
### Root Cause

Stuttering OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7 via `aiin`) re-send stream frames; the shared adapter mishandled both shapes: `_dedupeOverlap` trimmed overlaps only for `k >= 2`, so a 1-char punctuation stutter survived (doubled punctuation in thinking), and `_ensureToolCallBlock` matched blocks only by `streamIndex`/`id`, so a re-sent call frame with a fresh id spawned a second identical block and executed the command twice.

### Fix

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`:
  - `_dedupeOverlap`: trim 1-char overlaps too, with an ellipsis guard (a delta repeating its leading char is a legit `...` continuation, not a seam); full-snapshot branch and 64-char window unchanged.
  - `_ensureToolCallBlock` + new `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: on a lookup miss, a frame whose name equals the last registered block's name with `partialArgs` empty or a prefix of the incoming args is a re-send — merge into that block (newer id adopted only if the old is empty), appending only the non-overlapping argument suffix.

### Test Coverage

- `test/providers/openai_completions_test.dart`: stutter-trim (`greeting`, `.`, `.` → `greeting. I should`), ellipsis intact (`hmm`, `.`, `..` → `hmm...`), re-sent frame with fresh id → ONE block/one execution, distinct calls → two blocks. All failed-before/green-after as specified.
- Existing sliding-window fixture updated: `'Продолжжжжаем'` → `'Продолжжжаем'` (it baked in the surviving 1-char stutter); clean-delta cases byte-identical (C4).
- Full suite: 6549 passed, 19 failed — all 19 verified pre-existing on the clean base commit (`124f1e0`) via a detached worktree run (env-dependent PTY/CLI suites already red on main per gh-1649); provider suites: 827/827 green.

### Notes

- Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction.
- AC4 (live `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7` check) is not executable in this environment; the fixtures reproduce both observed defects at the adapter level.

+name: android-ndk-preinstall
+description: >-
+  Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK so Gradle configuration never
+  triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download mid-build. gh-1655: one
+  truncated android-ndk-r28c-linux download ("Error on ZipFile unknown
+  archive" at 33%) red'd the ci.yml build-android leg — and the aggregate
+  Quality gate with it — because AGP's in-configuration auto-install path
+  has NO retry. The NDK version is resolved from the pinned Flutter SDK's
+  own gradle plugin source (the exact value flutter.ndkVersion resolves
+  to — no second pin to drift), the install is skipped when the NDK is
+  already present, and the download itself is bounded-retried — the same
+  hardening the flutter_gemma Android seed carries (gh-1468). Companion
+  guard: test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart.
+runs:
+  using: composite
+  steps:
+    - name: Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK (bounded retry)
+      shell: bash
+      run: |
+        set -euo pipefail
+        # flutter.ndkVersion's single source of truth: the gradle plugin
+        # bundled with the SDK flutter-action installed. app/
+        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so
+        # resolving here can never skew from what AGP requests at
+        # configuration time (a literal pin on either side would break
+        # that coupling — the guard test pins both sides).
+        if [ -n "${FLUTTER_ROOT:-}" ]; then
+          FLUTTER_HOME="$FLUTTER_ROOT"
+        else
+          FLUTTER_BIN="$(command -v flutter || true)"
+          if [ -z "$FLUTTER_BIN" ]; then
+            echo "::error::cannot locate flutter (set FLUTTER_ROOT) — the NDK pre-install resolves the version from the SDK's gradle plugin source"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          FLUTTER_HOME="$(dirname "$(dirname "$FLUTTER_BIN")")"
+        fi
+        GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_HOME/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"
+        NDK_VERSION="$(grep -hoE 'val ndkVersion: String = "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"' "$GRADLE_SRC" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)"
+        if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
+          echo "::error::cannot resolve flutter.ndkVersion from $GRADLE_SRC — the Flutter gradle plugin layout moved; update the extraction in .github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall (and test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart) TOGETHER"
+          exit 1
+        fi
+        echo "resolved flutter.ndkVersion = $NDK_VERSION"
+        ANDROID_SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-/usr/local/lib/android/sdk}"
+        SDKMANAGER="$ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
+        if [ ! -x "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
+          SDKMANAGER="$(command -v sdkmanager || true)"
+        fi
+        if [ -z "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
+          echo "::error::sdkmanager not found (expected $ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager) — the NDK pre-install needs the Android cmdline-tools"
+          exit 1
+        fi
+        # Idempotence: AGP resolves `ndkVersion` against
+        # $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/<version> — source.properties present means
+        # the NDK is fully installed; skip the download entirely.
+        if [ -f "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties" ]; then
+          echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION already installed — skipping pre-install"
+          exit 0
+        fi
+        # Accept any license the image has not pre-accepted so the
+        # installs below never prompt (|| true: `yes` dies of SIGPIPE by
+        # design once sdkmanager stops reading).
+        yes | "$SDKMANAGER" --licenses > /dev/null || true
+        # gh-1655: Gradle's own auto-install (the same sdkmanager call,
+        # run inside configuration) has no retry — one truncated download
+        # unzips as "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" and the build dies.
+        # Here the same download gets three attempts with backoff.
+        for attempt in 1 2 3; do
+          echo "installing NDK $NDK_VERSION (attempt $attempt/3)"
+          rm -rf "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION"
+          if "$SDKMANAGER" --install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION"; then
+            echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION installed"
+            exit 0
+          fi
+          echo "::warning::sdkmanager NDK install failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
+          sleep 10
+        done
+        echo "::error::NDK $NDK_VERSION install failed after 3 attempts — gh-1655 red'd the leg on a single truncated archive; inspect the sdkmanager output above"
+        exit 1

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1656
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1656
- **Title**: gh-1655 [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1655` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +726
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-16T14:03:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T11:24:06Z

## PR Description

Closes #1655
### Root Cause

Stuttering OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7 via `aiin`) re-send stream frames; the shared adapter mishandled both shapes: `_dedupeOverlap` trimmed overlaps only for `k >= 2`, so a 1-char punctuation stutter survived (doubled punctuation in thinking), and `_ensureToolCallBlock` matched blocks only by `streamIndex`/`id`, so a re-sent call frame with a fresh id spawned a second identical block and executed the command twice.

### Fix

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`:
  - `_dedupeOverlap`: trim 1-char overlaps too, with an ellipsis guard (a delta repeating its leading char is a legit `...` continuation, not a seam); full-snapshot branch and 64-char window unchanged.
  - `_ensureToolCallBlock` + new `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: on a lookup miss, a frame whose name equals the last registered block's name with `partialArgs` empty or a prefix of the incoming args is a re-send — merge into that block (newer id adopted only if the old is empty), appending only the non-overlapping argument suffix.

### Test Coverage

- `test/providers/openai_completions_test.dart`: stutter-trim (`greeting`, `.`, `.` → `greeting. I should`), ellipsis intact (`hmm`, `.`, `..` → `hmm...`), re-sent frame with fresh id → ONE block/one execution, distinct calls → two blocks. All failed-before/green-after as specified.
- Existing sliding-window fixture updated: `'Продолжжжжаем'` → `'Продолжжжаем'` (it baked in the surviving 1-char stutter); clean-delta cases byte-identical (C4).
- Full suite: 6549 passed, 19 failed — all 19 verified pre-existing on the clean base commit (`124f1e0`) via a detached worktree run (env-dependent PTY/CLI suites already red on main per gh-1649); provider suites: 827/827 green.

### Notes

- Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction.
- AC4 (live `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7` check) is not executable in this environment; the fixtures reproduce both observed defects at the adapter level.

+name: android-ndk-preinstall
+description: >-
+  Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK so Gradle configuration never
+  triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download mid-build. gh-1655: one

+  has NO retry. The NDK version is resolved from the pinned Flutter SDK's
+  own gradle plugin source (the exact value flutter.ndkVersion resolves
+  to — no second pin to drift), the install is skipped when the NDK is
+  already present, and the download itself is bounded-retried — the same
+  hardening the flutter_gemma Android seed carries (gh-1468). Companion
+  guard: test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart.
+runs:
+  using: composite
+  steps:
+    - name: Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK (bounded retry)
+      shell: bash
+      run: |
+        set -euo pipefail
+        # flutter.ndkVersion's single source of truth: the gradle plugin
+        # bundled with the SDK flutter-action installed. app/
+        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so
+        # resolving here can never skew from what AGP requests at
+        # configuration time (a literal pin on either side would break
+        # that coupling — the guard test pins both sides).
+        if [ -n "${FLUTTER_ROOT:-}" ]; then
+          FLUTTER_HOME="$FLUTTER_ROOT"
+        else
+          FLUTTER_BIN="$(command -v flutter || true)"
+          if [ -z "$FLUTTER_BIN" ]; then
+            echo "::error::cannot locate flutter (set FLUTTER_ROOT) — the NDK pre-install resolves the version from the SDK's gradle plugin source"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          FLUTTER_HOME="$(dirname "$(dirname "$FLUTTER_BIN")")"
+        fi
+        GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_HOME/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"
+        NDK_VERSION="$(grep -hoE 'val ndkVersion: String = "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"' "$GRADLE_SRC" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)"
+        if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
+          echo "::error::cannot resolve flutter.ndkVersion from $GRADLE_SRC — the Flutter gradle plugin layout moved; update the extraction in .github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall (and test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart) TOGETHER"
+          exit 1
+        fi
+        echo "resolved flutter.ndkVersion = $NDK_VERSION"
+        ANDROID_SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-/usr/local/lib/android/sdk}"
+        SDKMANAGER="$ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
+        if [ ! -x "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
+          SDKMANAGER="$(command -v sdkmanager || true)"
+        fi
+        if [ -z "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
+          echo "::error::sdkmanager not found (expected $ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager) — the NDK pre-install needs the Android cmdline-tools"
+          exit 1
+        fi
+        # Idempotence: AGP resolves `ndkVersion` against
+        # $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/<version> — source.properties present means
+        # the NDK is fully installed; skip the download entirely.
+        if [ -f "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties" ]; then
+          echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION already installed — skipping pre-install"
+          exit 0
+        fi
+        # Accept any license the image has not pre-accepted so the
+        # installs below never prompt (|| true: `yes` dies of SIGPIPE by
+        # design once sdkmanager stops reading).
+        yes | "$SDKMANAGER" --licenses > /dev/null || true
+        # gh-1655: Gradle's own auto-install (the same sdkmanager call,
+        # run inside configuration) has no retry — one truncated download
+        # unzips as "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" and the build dies.
+        # Here the same download gets three attempts with backoff.
+        for attempt in 1 2 3; do

+          rm -rf "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION"
+          if "$SDKMANAGER" --install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION"; then
+            echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION installed"
+            exit 0
+          fi
+          echo "::warning::sdkmanager NDK install failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
+          sleep 10
+        done
+        echo "::error::NDK $NDK_VERSION install failed after 3 attempts — gh-1655 red'd the leg on a single truncated archive; inspect the sdkmanager output above"
+        exit 1

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1656
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1656
- **Title**: gh-1655 [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1655` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +726
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-16T14:03:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T11:24:06Z

## PR Description

Closes #1655
### Root Cause

Stuttering OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7 via `aiin`) re-send stream frames; the shared adapter mishandled both shapes: `_dedupeOverlap` trimmed overlaps only for `k >= 2`, so a 1-char punctuation stutter survived (doubled punctuation in thinking), and `_ensureToolCallBlock` matched blocks only by `streamIndex`/`id`, so a re-sent call frame with a fresh id spawned a second identical block and executed the command twice.

### Fix

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`:
  - `_dedupeOverlap`: trim 1-char overlaps too, with an ellipsis guard (a delta repeating its leading char is a legit `...` continuation, not a seam); full-snapshot branch and 64-char window unchanged.
  - `_ensureToolCallBlock` + new `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: on a lookup miss, a frame whose name equals the last registered block's name with `partialArgs` empty or a prefix of the incoming args is a re-send — merge into that block (newer id adopted only if the old is empty), appending only the non-overlapping argument suffix.

### Test Coverage

- `test/providers/openai_completions_test.dart`: stutter-trim (`greeting`, `.`, `.` → `greeting. I should`), ellipsis intact (`hmm`, `.`, `..` → `hmm...`), re-sent frame with fresh id → ONE block/one execution, distinct calls → two blocks. All failed-before/green-after as specified.
- Existing sliding-window fixture updated: `'Продолжжжжаем'` → `'Продолжжжаем'` (it baked in the surviving 1-char stutter); clean-delta cases byte-identical (C4).
- Full suite: 6549 passed, 19 failed — all 19 verified pre-existing on the clean base commit (`124f1e0`) via a detached worktree run (env-dependent PTY/CLI suites already red on main per gh-1649); provider suites: 827/827 green.

### Notes

- Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction.
- AC4 (live `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7` check) is not executable in this environment; the fixtures reproduce both observed defects at the adapter level.

+name: android-ndk-preinstall
+description: >-
+  Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK so Gradle configuration never
+  triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download mid-build. gh-1655: one
+  truncated android-ndk-r28c-linux download ("Error on ZipFile unknown
+  archive" at 33%) red'd the ci.yml build-android leg — and the aggregate
+  Quality gate with it — because AGP's in-configuration auto-install path
+  has NO retry. The NDK version is resolved from the pinned Flutter SDK's
+  own gradle plugin source (the exact value flutter.ndkVersion resolves
+  to — no second pin to drift), the install is skipped when the NDK is
+  already present, and the download itself is bounded-retried — the same
+  hardening the flutter_gemma Android seed carries (gh-1468). Companion
+  guard: test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart.
+runs:
+  using: composite
+  steps:
+    - name: Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK (bounded retry)
+      shell: bash
+      run: |
+        set -euo pipefail
+        # flutter.ndkVersion's single source of truth: the gradle plugin
+        # bundled with the SDK flutter-action installed. app/
+        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so
+        # resolving here can never skew from what AGP requests at
+        # configuration time (a literal pin on either side would break
+        # that coupling — the guard test pins both sides).
+        if [ -n "${FLUTTER_ROOT:-}" ]; then
+          FLUTTER_HOME="$FLUTTER_ROOT"
+        else
+          FLUTTER_BIN="$(command -v flutter || true)"
+          if [ -z "$FLUTTER_BIN" ]; then
+            echo "::error::cannot locate flutter (set FLUTTER_ROOT) — the NDK pre-install resolves the version from the SDK's gradle plugin source"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          FLUTTER_HOME="$(dirname "$(dirname "$FLUTTER_BIN")")"
+        fi
+        GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_HOME/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"
+        NDK_VERSION="$(grep -hoE 'val ndkVersion: String = "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"' "$GRADLE_SRC" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)"
+        if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
+          echo "::error::cannot resolve flutter.ndkVersion from $GRADLE_SRC — the Flutter gradle plugin layout moved; update the extraction in .github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall (and test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart) TOGETHER"
+          exit 1
+        fi
+        echo "resolved flutter.ndkVersion = $NDK_VERSION"
+        ANDROID_SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-/usr/local/lib/android/sdk}"
+        SDKMANAGER="$ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
+        if [ ! -x "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
+          SDKMANAGER="$(command -v sdkmanager || true)"
+        fi
+        if [ -z "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
+          echo "::error::sdkmanager not found (expected $ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager) — the NDK pre-install needs the Android cmdline-tools"
+          exit 1
+        fi
+        # Idempotence: AGP resolves `ndkVersion` against
+        # $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/<version> — source.properties present means
+        # the NDK is fully installed; skip the download entirely.
+        if [ -f "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties" ]; then
+          echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION already installed — skipping pre-install"
+          exit 0
+        fi

+        # installs below never prompt (|| true: `yes` dies of SIGPIPE by
+        # design once sdkmanager stops reading).
+        yes | "$SDKMANAGER" --licenses > /dev/null || true

Now let me think about correctness of the adapter changes:

1. `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: It looks at the LAST ToolCallStreamingBlock in `blocks`. It matches only by name equality, and args prefix. There's a potential issue: consider two sequential DIFFERENT calls to the same tool within a single message, e.g. first call `bash {"command":"ls"}` completes (block1 name='bash', args complete), then the model sends a SECOND frame `bash {"command":"pwd"}` — with a fresh id. `_lookupToolCallBlock(streamIndex, id)`: if no index given, lookup by id misses (fresh id). Then `_matchResentToolCallBlock` is called — last block has name 'bash' matching; existing args is `'{"command":"ls"}'`, incoming args `'{"command":"pwd"}'` — `'{"command":"pwd"}'.startsWith('{"command":"ls"}')` is false → returns null. Good, guard works. But consider the second call with a name prefix overlap: `'{"command":"ls"}'` then second call `'{"command":"ls -la"}'` — startsWith is TRUE → the two distinct calls get MERGED! The second call `{"command":"ls -la"}` would be merged into the first block, appending only ` -la"}`... wait let's trace: `_matchResentToolCallBlock` returns last block. Then in `_handleSingleToolCallDelta` with resend != null: existing = `'{"command":"ls"}'`; toolDelta = `'{"command":"ls -la"}'`; startsWith(existing) → toolDelta = `' -la"}'`; writes to block.partialArgs → `{"command":"ls -la"}` — hmm actually that produces correct JSON? `{"command":"ls"}` + ` -la"}` = `{"command":"ls -la"}`. Ha, it accidentally reconstructs the second call's args but inside the FIRST block, meaning the first call's args are now the second's — block1 now says `ls -la` instead of `ls`. And ToolCallEndEvent fires only for... let me check how ends are emitted. Actually the tool call end events are emitted at finish presumably by iterating blocks. So the merge results in ONE ToolCallEndEvent with args `ls -la` — the original `ls` call got overwritten in effect. So two genuinely distinct sequential calls where one call's arguments happen to be a prefix-extension of the previous call's arguments (e.g. `ls` then `ls -la`, `cat file` then `cat file.txt`?) would be incorrectly merged.

Wait — but is the prefix guard sufficient in practice? The prefix case: second call `"{"command":"ls"}"` and `"{"command":"ls -l"}"`. `args.startsWith(existing)` — existing is `{"command":"ls"}`; incoming `{"command":"ls -l"}` starts with `{"command":"ls`... hmm `{"command":"ls -l"}` — does it start with `{"command":"ls"}`? The existing ends with `"` after `ls`, and incoming has ` -l` after `ls` — so no, `ls"` vs `ls ` differ at that position. Actually `{"command":"ls"}` is 17 chars; `{"command":"ls -l"}` first 17 chars = `{"command":"ls -l` — differs at index 16 (`"` vs `). So NOT a prefix. Hmm, prefix requires incoming to literally begin with the full existing string including closing quote/brace. E.g. call1 `{"command":"ls"}` and call2 `{"command":"ls"}...` — can't be since JSON starts with `{`. For incoming args to start with existing `{"command":"ls"}` it would need to start with `{"command":"ls"}` followed by more — but that's invalid JSON unless it's like `{"command":"ls"}` + more keys... e.g. `{"command":"ls","other":1}` — incoming starts with `{"command":"ls"` but existing includes the `}`: `{"command":"ls"}` — incoming `{"command":"ls","other":1}` starts with `{"command":"ls"` but not `{"command":"ls"}` since char 16 is `,` vs `}`. Hmm wait, actually could a relay send call1 args = `{"command":"ls"}` and call2 args = `{"command":"ls"}` + extra... The args string of a re-sent frame is the FULL args repeated (per gh-1655). For a genuinely different second call with same tool name, args would rarely literally start with the full previous args string. The realistic collision: two calls with identical prefix keys where the first is a strict prefix: existing = `{"command":"ls` (incomplete? no, blocks complete at finish). At finish blocks are complete.

Edge: call1 args = `{"command":"ls"}`, call2 args = `{"command":"ls"}` — identical — that IS ambiguous with a re-send; can't distinguish anyway. Fine.

Another edge: what if call2 has MORE arguments where existing is a strict JSON prefix? e.g. call1 = `{"command":"ls"}` and call2 = `{"command":"ls"}` — only identical works in valid JSON world... Actually what about call1 = `{"command":"ls", "cwd":"/a"}` truncated? Not realistic. OK.

But there's another subtler issue: `_matchResentToolCallBlock` matches the LAST registered block regardless of whether the last block is already COMPLETE (closed by a subsequent frame?) — but blocks don't close mid-stream; at finish all blocks emit ends. Fine.

More significant: what if the re-sent frame has the same id but no `index`? Then `_lookupToolCallBlock` by id hits and resend logic doesn't fire. Fine.

What about a scenario where the relay re-sends the frame but the previous block was for the same tool name and `existing` is empty (name arrived in an earlier delta, args not yet)? existing empty → match. Then incoming args start with existing (empty) → suffix = full args → written once. Good.

What about the case where the resent frame's args are a strict prefix of existing (relay sent MORE args first time, then re-sends a shorter snapshot)? `existing.isNotEmpty && !args.startsWith(existing)` → returns null → falls to `_ensureToolCallBlock` → lookup miss → creates a SECOND block with same name → duplicate execution. This is the sliding-window relay shape! For thinking they handle overlap trimming; for tool calls, a stuttering relay could plausibly re-send the same frame with args being an overlap/prefix of accumulated. E.g. block accumulated `{"command":"js hello.js}` (missing close) then re-sent frame arrives with `{"command":"js hello.js"}` (full). existing = `{"command":"js hello.js}` (19 chars without `"}`), args = `{"command":"js hello.js"}`. args.startsWith(existing) → true (args begins with existing). → merge, suffix = `"}` appended. Actually wait — think again about what stuttering relays do: re-send stream frames; a re-sent frame is a full frame identical to one already processed. The fresh-id full repeat is handled. A sliding-window tool-call shape (partial resend) would break existing relays anyway (args would double-append). This is a new capability only for full repeats. I'd call it a SUGGESTION-level doc note.

And block == resent. So `toolDelta.startsWith(existing)` is guaranteed; the inner if is redundant but harmless. Fine.

But: `if (toolDelta.isEmpty) return;` — this returns early WITHOUT pushing the ToolCallDeltaEvent. Is that OK? A zero-length delta event is useless, so skipping is fine. But it also skips `_applyToolCallIdentity`? No — identity was applied before. OK.

One more: `_applyToolCallIdentity(block, rawToolCall)` — "newer id adopted only if the old is empty": block.id non-empty → resent frame's new id NOT registered in `toolCallBlocksById`. That means if yet ANOTHER frame arrives referencing the new id (e.g. relay sends frame1 id=A, frame2 id=B (resend), then frame3 id=B with more args), lookup by id B misses, but `_matchResentToolCallBlock` matches last block by name+prefix → merges. However, there's an issue: `pendingReasoningDetailsByToolCallId` and `thoughtSignature` matching by id — a resent id B never maps to the block; encrypted reasoning details keyed by B would be stored pending forever and never attached. Minor edge; Anthropic-style encrypted reasoning on OpenAI-compat relays is rare. Suggestion level.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1656
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1656
- **Title**: gh-1655 [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1655` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +726
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-16T14:03:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T11:24:06Z

## PR Description

Closes #1655
### Root Cause

Stuttering OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7 via `aiin`) re-send stream frames; the shared adapter mishandled both shapes: `_dedupeOverlap` trimmed overlaps only for `k >= 2`, so a 1-char punctuation stutter survived (doubled punctuation in thinking), and `_ensureToolCallBlock` matched blocks only by `streamIndex`/`id`, so a re-sent call frame with a fresh id spawned a second identical block and executed the command twice.

### Fix

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`:
  - `_dedupeOverlap`: trim 1-char overlaps too, with an ellipsis guard (a delta repeating its leading char is a legit `...` continuation, not a seam); full-snapshot branch and 64-char window unchanged.
  - `_ensureToolCallBlock` + new `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: on a lookup miss, a frame whose name equals the last registered block's name with `partialArgs` empty or a prefix of the incoming args is a re-send — merge into that block (newer id adopted only if the old is empty), appending only the non-overlapping argument suffix.

### Test Coverage

- `test/providers/openai_completions_test.dart`: stutter-trim (`greeting`, `.`, `.` → `greeting. I should`), ellipsis intact (`hmm`, `.`, `..` → `hmm...`), re-sent frame with fresh id → ONE block/one execution, distinct calls → two blocks. All failed-before/green-after as specified.
- Existing sliding-window fixture updated: `'Продолжжжжаем'` → `'Продолжжжаем'` (it baked in the surviving 1-char stutter); clean-delta cases byte-identical (C4).
- Full suite: 6549 passed, 19 failed — all 19 verified pre-existing on the clean base commit (`124f1e0`) via a detached worktree run (env-dependent PTY/CLI suites already red on main per gh-1649); provider suites: 827/827 green.

### Notes

- Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction.
- AC4 (live `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7` check) is not executable in this environment; the fixtures reproduce both observed defects at the adapter level.

+name: android-ndk-preinstall
+description: >-
+  Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK so Gradle configuration never
+  triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download mid-build. gh-1655: one
+  truncated android-ndk-r28c-linux download ("Error on ZipFile unknown
+  archive" at 33%) red'd the ci.yml build-android leg — and the aggregate
+  Quality gate with it — because AGP's in-configuration auto-install path
+  has NO retry. The NDK version is resolved from the pinned Flutter SDK's
+  own gradle plugin source (the exact value flutter.ndkVersion resolves
+  to — no second pin to drift), the install is skipped when the NDK is
+  already present, and the download itself is bounded-retried — the same
+  hardening the flutter_gemma Android seed carries (gh-1468). Companion
+  guard: test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart.
+runs:
+  using: composite
+  steps:
+    - name: Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK (bounded retry)
+      shell: bash
+      run: |
+        set -euo pipefail
+        # flutter.ndkVersion's single source of truth: the gradle plugin
+        # bundled with the SDK flutter-action installed. app/
+        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so
+        # resolving here can never skew from what AGP requests at
+        # configuration time (a literal pin on either side would break
+        # that coupling — the guard test pins both sides).
+        if [ -n "${FLUTTER_ROOT:-}" ]; then
+          FLUTTER_HOME="$FLUTTER_ROOT"
+        else
+          FLUTTER_BIN="$(command -v flutter || true)"
+          if [ -z "$FLUTTER_BIN" ]; then
+            echo "::error::cannot locate flutter (set FLUTTER_ROOT) — the NDK pre-install resolves the version from the SDK's gradle plugin source"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          FLUTTER_HOME="$(dirname "$(dirname "$FLUTTER_BIN")")"
+        fi
+        GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_HOME/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"
+        NDK_VERSION="$(grep -hoE 'val ndkVersion: String = "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"' "$GRADLE_SRC" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)"
+        if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
+          echo "::error::cannot resolve flutter.ndkVersion from $GRADLE_SRC — the Flutter gradle plugin layout moved; update the extraction in .github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall (and test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart) TOGETHER"
+          exit 1
+        fi
+        echo "resolved flutter.ndkVersion = $NDK_VERSION"
+        ANDROID_SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-/usr/local/lib/android/sdk}"
+        SDKMANAGER="$ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
+        if [ ! -x "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
+          SDKMANAGER="$(command -v sdkmanager || true)"
+        fi
+        if [ -z "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
+          echo "::error::sdkmanager not found (expected $ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager) — the NDK pre-install needs the Android cmdline-tools"
+          exit 1
+        fi
+        # Idempotence: AGP resolves `ndkVersion` against
+        # $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/<version> — source.properties present means
+        # the NDK is fully installed; skip the download entirely.
+        if [ -f "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties" ]; then
+          echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION already installed — skipping pre-install"
+          exit 0
+        fi
+        # Accept any license the image has not pre-accepted so the
+        # installs below never prompt (|| true: `yes` dies of SIGPIPE by
+        # design once sdkmanager stops reading).
+        yes | "$SDKMANAGER" --licenses > /dev/null || true
+        # gh-1655: Gradle's own auto-install (the same sdkmanager call,
+        # run inside configuration) has no retry — one truncated download
+        # unzips as "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" and the build dies.
+        # Here the same download gets three attempts with backoff.
+        for attempt in 1 2 3; do
+          echo "installing NDK $NDK_VERSION (attempt $attempt/3)"
+          rm -rf "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION"
+          if "$SDKMANAGER" --install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION"; then
+            echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION installed"
+            exit 0
+          fi
+          echo "::warning::sdkmanager NDK install failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
+          sleep 10
+        done
+        echo "::error::NDK $NDK_VERSION install failed after 3 attempts — gh-1655 red'd the leg on a single truncated archive; inspect the sdkmanager output above"
+        exit 1

## PR Description

Closes #1655
### Root Cause

Stuttering OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7 via `aiin`) re-send stream frames; the shared adapter mishandled both shapes: `_dedupeOverlap` trimmed overlaps only for `k >= 2`, so a 1-char punctuation stutter survived (doubled punctuation in thinking), and `_ensureToolCallBlock` matched blocks only by `streamIndex`/`id`, so a re-sent call frame with a fresh id spawned a second identical block and executed the command twice.

### Fix

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`:
  - `_dedupeOverlap`: trim 1-char overlaps too, with an ellipsis guard (a delta repeating its leading char is a legit `...` continuation, not a seam); full-snapshot branch and 64-char window unchanged.
  - `_ensureToolCallBlock` + new `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: on a lookup miss, a frame whose name equals the last registered block's name with `partialArgs` empty or a prefix of the incoming args is a re-send — merge into that block (newer id adopted only if the old is empty), appending only the non-overlapping argument suffix.

### Test Coverage

- `test/providers/openai_completions_test.dart`: stutter-trim (`greeting`, `.`, `.` → `greeting. I should`), ellipsis intact (`hmm`, `.`, `..` → `hmm...`), re-sent frame with fresh id → ONE block/one execution, distinct calls → two blocks. All failed-before/green-after as specified.
- Existing sliding-window fixture updated: `'Продолжжжжаем'` → `'Продолжжжаем'` (it baked in the surviving 1-char stutter); clean-delta cases byte-identical (C4).
- Full suite: 6549 passed, 19 failed — all 19 verified pre-existing on the clean base commit (`124f1e0`) via a detached worktree run (env-dependent PTY/CLI suites already red on main per gh-1649); provider suites: 827/827 green.

### Notes

- Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction.
- AC4 (live `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7` check) is not executable in this environment; the fixtures reproduce both observed defects at the adapter level.

+name: android-ndk-preinstall
+description: >-
+  Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK so Gradle configuration never
+  triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download mid-build. gh-1655: one
+  truncated android-ndk-r28c-linux download ("Error on ZipFile unknown
+  archive" at 33%) red'd the ci.yml build-android leg — and the aggregate
+  Quality gate with it — because AGP's in-configuration auto-install path
+  has NO retry. The NDK version is resolved from the pinned Flutter SDK's
+  own gradle plugin source (the exact value flutter.ndkVersion resolves
+  to — no second pin to drift), the install is skipped when the NDK is
+  already present, and the download itself is bounded-retried — the same
+  hardening the flutter_gemma Android seed carries (gh-1468). Companion
+  guard: test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart.
+runs:
+  using: composite
+  steps:
+    - name: Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK (bounded retry)
+      shell: bash
+      run: |
+        set -euo pipefail
+        # flutter.ndkVersion's single source of truth: the gradle plugin
+        # bundled with the SDK flutter-action installed. app/
+        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so
+        # resolving here can never skew from what AGP requests at
+        # configuration time (a literal pin on either side would break
+        # that coupling — the guard test pins both sides).
+        if [ -n "${FLUTTER_ROOT:-}" ]; then
+          FLUTTER_HOME="$FLUTTER_ROOT"
+        else
+          FLUTTER_BIN="$(command -v flutter || true)"
+          if [ -z "$FLUTTER_BIN" ]; then
+            echo "::error::cannot locate flutter (set FLUTTER_ROOT) — the NDK pre-install resolves the version from the SDK's gradle plugin source"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          FLUTTER_HOME="$(dirname "$(dirname "$FLUTTER_BIN")")"
+        fi
+        GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_HOME/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"
+        NDK_VERSION="$(grep -hoE 'val ndkVersion: String = "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"' "$GRADLE_SRC" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)"
+        if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
+          echo "::error::cannot resolve flutter.ndkVersion from $GRADLE_SRC — the Flutter gradle plugin layout moved; update the extraction in .github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall (and test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart) TOGETHER"
+          exit 1
+        fi
+        echo "resolved flutter.ndkVersion = $NDK_VERSION"
+        ANDROID_SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-/usr/local/lib/android/sdk}"
+        SDKMANAGER="$ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
+        if [ ! -x "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
+          SDKMANAGER="$(command -v sdkmanager || true)"
+        fi
+        if [ -z "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
+          echo "::error::sdkmanager not found (expected $ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager) — the NDK pre-install needs the Android cmdline-tools"
+          exit 1
+        fi
+        # Idempotence: AGP resolves `ndkVersion` against
+        # $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/<version> — source.properties present means
+        # the NDK is fully installed; skip the download entirely.
+        if [ -f "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties" ]; then
+          echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION already installed — skipping pre-install"
+          exit 0
+        fi
+        # Accept any license the image has not pre-accepted so the
+        # installs below never prompt (|| true: `yes` dies of SIGPIPE by
+        # design once sdkmanager stops reading).
+        yes | "$SDKMANAGER" --licenses > /dev/null || true
+        # gh-1655: Gradle's own auto-install (the same sdkmanager call,
+        # run inside configuration) has no retry — one truncated download
+        # unzips as "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" and the build dies.
+        # Here the same download gets three attempts with backoff.
+        for attempt in 1 2 3; do

+          rm -rf "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION"
+          if "$SDKMANAGER" --install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION"; then
+            echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION installed"
+            exit 0
+          fi
+          echo "::warning::sdkmanager NDK install failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
+          sleep 10
+        done
+        echo "::error::NDK $NDK_VERSION install failed after 3 attempts — gh-1655 red'd the leg on a single truncated archive; inspect the sdkmanager output above"
+        exit 1

Now let me think about correctness of the adapter changes:

1. `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: It looks at the LAST ToolCallStreamingBlock in `blocks`. It matches only by name equality, and args prefix. There's a potential issue: consider two sequential DIFFERENT calls to the same tool within a single message, e.g. first call `bash {"command":"ls"}` completes (block1 name='bash', args complete), then the model sends a SECOND frame `bash {"command":"pwd"}` — with a fresh id. `_lookupToolCallBlock(streamIndex, id)`: if no index given, lookup by id misses (fresh id). Then `_matchResentToolCallBlock` is called — last block has name 'bash' matching; existing args is `'{"command":"ls"}'`, incoming args `'{"command":"pwd"}'` — `'{"command":"pwd"}'.startsWith('{"command":"ls"}')` is false → returns null. Good, guard works. But consider the second call with a name prefix overlap: `'{"command":"ls"}'` then second call `'{"command":"ls -la"}'` — startsWith is TRUE → the two distinct calls get MERGED! The second call `{"command":"ls -la"}` would be merged into the first block, appending only ` -la"}`... wait let's trace: `_matchResentToolCallBlock` returns last block. Then in `_handleSingleToolCallDelta` with resend != null: existing = `'{"command":"ls"}'`; toolDelta = `'{"command":"ls -la"}'`; startsWith(existing) → toolDelta = `' -la"}'`; writes to block.partialArgs → `{"command":"ls -la"}` — hmm actually that produces correct JSON? `{"command":"ls"}` + ` -la"}` = `{"command":"ls -la"}`. Ha, it accidentally reconstructs the second call's args but inside the FIRST block, meaning the first call's args are now the second's — block1 now says `ls -la` instead of `ls`. And ToolCallEndEvent fires only for... let me check how ends are emitted. Actually the tool call end events are emitted at finish presumably by iterating blocks. So the merge results in ONE ToolCallEndEvent with args `ls -la` — the original `ls` call got overwritten in effect. So two genuinely distinct sequential calls where one call's arguments happen to be a prefix-extension of the previous call's arguments (e.g. `ls` then `ls -la`, `cat file` then `cat file.txt`?) would be incorrectly merged.

Wait — but is the prefix guard sufficient in practice? The prefix case: second call `"{"command":"ls"}"` and `"{"command":"ls -l"}"`. `args.startsWith(existing)` — existing is `{"command":"ls"}`; incoming `{"command":"ls -l"}` starts with `{"command":"ls`... hmm `{"command":"ls -l"}` — does it start with `{"command":"ls"}`? The existing ends with `"` after `ls`, and incoming has ` -l` after `ls` — so no, `ls"` vs `ls ` differ at that position. Actually `{"command":"ls"}` is 17 chars; `{"command":"ls -l"}` first 17 chars = `{"command":"ls -l` — differs at index 16 (`"` vs `). So NOT a prefix. Hmm, prefix requires incoming to literally begin with the full existing string including closing quote/brace. E.g. call1 `{"command":"ls"}` and call2 `{"command":"ls"}...` — can't be since JSON starts with `{`. For incoming args to start with existing `{"command":"ls"}` it would need to start with `{"command":"ls"}` followed by more — but that's invalid JSON unless it's like `{"command":"ls"}` + more keys... e.g. `{"command":"ls","other":1}` — incoming starts with `{"command":"ls"` but existing includes the `}`: `{"command":"ls"}` — incoming `{"command":"ls","other":1}` starts with `{"command":"ls"` but not `{"command":"ls"}` since char 16 is `,` vs `}`. Hmm wait, actually could a relay send call1 args = `{"command":"ls"}` and call2 args = `{"command":"ls"}` + extra... The args string of a re-sent frame is the FULL args repeated (per gh-1655). For a genuinely different second call with same tool name, args would rarely literally start with the full previous args string. The realistic collision: two calls with identical prefix keys where the first is a strict prefix: existing = `{"command":"ls` (incomplete? no, blocks complete at finish). At finish blocks are complete.

Edge: call1 args = `{"command":"ls"}`, call2 args = `{"command":"ls"}` — identical — that IS ambiguous with a re-send; can't distinguish anyway. Fine.

Another edge: what if call2 has MORE arguments where existing is a strict JSON prefix? e.g. call1 = `{"command":"ls"}` and call2 = `{"command":"ls"}` — only identical works in valid JSON world... Actually what about call1 = `{"command":"ls", "cwd":"/a"}` truncated? Not realistic. OK.

But there's another subtler issue: `_matchResentToolCallBlock` matches the LAST registered block regardless of whether the last block is already COMPLETE (closed by a subsequent frame?) — but blocks don't close mid-stream; at finish all blocks emit ends. Fine.

More significant: what if the re-sent frame has the same id but no `index`? Then `_lookupToolCallBlock` by id hits and resend logic doesn't fire. Fine.

What about a scenario where the relay re-sends the frame but the previous block was for the same tool name and `existing` is empty (name arrived in an earlier delta, args not yet)? existing empty → match. Then incoming args start with existing (empty) → suffix = full args → written once. Good.

What about the case where the resent frame's args are a strict prefix of existing (relay sent MORE args first time, then re-sends a shorter snapshot)? `existing.isNotEmpty && !args.startsWith(existing)` → returns null → falls to `_ensureToolCallBlock` → lookup miss → creates a SECOND block with same name → duplicate execution. This is the sliding-window relay shape! For thinking they handle overlap trimming; for tool calls, a stuttering relay could plausibly re-send the same frame with args being an overlap/prefix of accumulated. E.g. block accumulated `{"command":"js hello.js}` (missing close) then re-sent frame arrives with `{"command":"js hello.js"}` (full). existing = `{"command":"js hello.js}` (19 chars without `"}`), args = `{"command":"js hello.js"}`. args.startsWith(existing) → true (args begins with existing). → merge, suffix = `"}` appended. Fine.

But sliding-window style: existing = `{"command":"js hello.js"}`, args = `hello.js"}` (window tail)? Then args doesn't start with existing → no match → second block → duplicate execution. Hmm — is that plausible? The PR description says relays re-send full frames. The thinking dedupe handles overlap windows; the tool-call merge handles only prefix-consistent shapes. Is this a BLOCKING gap? It's a robustness limitation; the stated defect shape (full re-send with fresh id) is fixed. I'd flag as SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT: extend the guard to also trim overlapping suffixes (`args` ending with existing, or longest common overlap) — or at least note the limitation in doc comment. Actually wait — think again about what stuttering relays do: re-send stream frames; a re-sent frame is a full frame identical to one already processed. The fresh-id full repeat is handled. A sliding-window tool-call shape (partial resend) would break existing relays anyway (args would double-append). This is a new capability only for full repeats. I'd call it a SUGGESTION-level doc note.

Now another correctness check on the merge path in `_handleSingleToolCallDelta`: if `resend != null` and incoming args do NOT start with existing — but wait, `_matchResentToolCallBlock` already guaranteed `existing.isEmpty || args.startsWith(existing)`. And block == resent. So `toolDelta.startsWith(existing)` is guaranteed; the inner if is redundant but harmless. Fine.

But: `if (toolDelta.isEmpty) return;` — this returns early WITHOUT pushing the ToolCallDeltaEvent. Is that OK? A zero-length delta event is useless, so skipping is fine. But it also skips `_applyToolCallIdentity`? No — identity was applied before. OK.

One more: `_applyToolCallIdentity(block, rawToolCall)` — "newer id adopted only if the old is empty": block.id non-empty → resent frame's new id NOT registered in `toolCallBlocksById`. That means if yet ANOTHER frame arrives referencing the new id (e.g. relay sends frame1 id=A, frame2 id=B (resend), then frame3 id=B with more args), lookup by id B misses, but `_matchResentToolCallBlock` matches last block by name+prefix → merges.       # one truncated download reds the scheduled leg.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall
        if: matrix.target == 'android'

      # Linux desktop toolchain + plugin native deps (gtk3 for the runner,
      # gstreamer for audioplayers_linux).
      - name: Install Linux desktop toolchain
        if: matrix.target == 'linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y clang cmake ninja-build pkg-config \
            libgtk-3-dev liblzma-dev libstdc++-12-dev \

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1656
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1656
- **Title**: gh-1655 [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1655` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +726
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-16T14:03:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T11:24:06Z

## PR Description

Closes #1655
### Root Cause

Stuttering OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7 via `aiin`) re-send stream frames; the shared adapter mishandled both shapes: `_dedupeOverlap` trimmed overlaps only for `k >= 2`, so a 1-char punctuation stutter survived (doubled punctuation in thinking), and `_ensureToolCallBlock` matched blocks only by `streamIndex`/`id`, so a re-sent call frame with a fresh id spawned a second identical block and executed the command twice.

### Fix

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`:
  - `_dedupeOverlap`: trim 1-char overlaps too, with an ellipsis guard (a delta repeating its leading char is a legit `...` continuation, not a seam); full-snapshot branch and 64-char window unchanged.
  - `_ensureToolCallBlock` + new `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: on a lookup miss, a frame whose name equals the last registered block's name with `partialArgs` empty or a prefix of the incoming args is a re-send — merge into that block (newer id adopted only if the old is empty), appending only the non-overlapping argument suffix.

### Test Coverage

- `test/providers/openai_completions_test.dart`: stutter-trim (`greeting`, `.`, `.` → `greeting. I should`), ellipsis intact (`hmm`, `.`, `..` → `hmm...`), re-sent frame with fresh id → ONE block/one execution, distinct calls → two blocks. All failed-before/green-after as specified.
- Existing sliding-window fixture updated: `'Продолжжжжаем'` → `'Продолжжжаем'` (it baked in the surviving 1-char stutter); clean-delta cases byte-identical (C4).
- Full suite: 6549 passed, 19 failed — all 19 verified pre-existing on the clean base commit (`124f1e0`) via a detached worktree run (env-dependent PTY/CLI suites already red on main per gh-1649); provider suites: 827/827 green.

### Notes

- Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction.
- AC4 (live `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7` check) is not executable in this environment; the fixtures reproduce both observed defects at the adapter level.

+name: android-ndk-preinstall
+description: >-
+  Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK so Gradle configuration never
+  triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download mid-build. gh-1655: one
+  truncated android-ndk-r28c-linux download ("Error on ZipFile unknown
+  archive" at 33%) red'd the ci.yml build-android leg — and the aggregate
+  Quality gate with it — because AGP's in-configuration auto-install path
+  has NO retry. The NDK version is resolved from the pinned Flutter SDK's
+  own gradle plugin source (the exact value flutter.ndkVersion resolves
+  to — no second pin to drift), the install is skipped when the NDK is
+  already present, and the download itself is bounded-retried — the same
+  hardening the flutter_gemma Android seed carries (gh-1468). Companion
+  guard: test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart.
+runs:
+  using: composite
+  steps:
+    - name: Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK (bounded retry)
+      shell: bash
+      run: |
+        set -euo pipefail
+        # flutter.ndkVersion's single source of truth: the gradle plugin
+        # bundled with the SDK flutter-action installed. app/
+        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so
+        # resolving here can never skew from what AGP requests at
+        # configuration time (a literal pin on either side would break
+        # that coupling — the guard test pins both sides).
+        if [ -n "${FLUTTER_ROOT:-}" ]; then
+          FLUTTER_HOME="$FLUTTER_ROOT"
+        else
+          FLUTTER_BIN="$(command -v flutter || true)"
+          if [ -z "$FLUTTER_BIN" ]; then
+            echo "::error::cannot locate flutter (set FLUTTER_ROOT) — the NDK pre-install resolves the version from the SDK's gradle plugin source"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          FLUTTER_HOME="$(dirname "$(dirname "$FLUTTER_BIN")")"
+        fi
+        GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_HOME/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"
+        NDK_VERSION="$(grep -hoE 'val ndkVersion: String = "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"' "$GRADLE_SRC" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)"
+        if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
+          echo "::error::cannot resolve flutter.ndkVersion from $GRADLE_SRC — the Flutter gradle plugin layout moved; update the extraction in .github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall (and test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart) TOGETHER"
+          exit 1
+        fi
+        echo "resolved flutter.ndkVersion = $NDK_VERSION"
+        ANDROID_SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-/usr/local/lib/android/sdk}"
+        SDKMANAGER="$ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
+        if [ ! -x "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
+          SDKMANAGER="$(command -v sdkmanager || true)"
+        fi
+        if [ -z "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
+          echo "::error::sdkmanager not found (expected $ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager) — the NDK pre-install needs the Android cmdline-tools"
+          exit 1
+        fi
+        # Idempotence: AGP resolves `ndkVersion` against
+        # $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/<version> — source.properties present means
+        # the NDK is fully installed; skip the download entirely.
+        if [ -f "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties" ]; then
+          echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION already installed — skipping pre-install"
+          exit 0
+        fi
+        # Accept any license the image has not pre-accepted so the
+        # installs below never prompt (|| true: `yes` dies of SIGPIPE by
+        # design once sdkmanager stops reading).
+        yes | "$SDKMANAGER" --licenses > /dev/null || true
+        # gh-1655: Gradle's own auto-install (the same sdkmanager call,
+        # run inside configuration) has no retry — one truncated download
+        # unzips as "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" and the build dies.
+        # Here the same download gets three attempts with backoff.
+        for attempt in 1 2 3; do
+          echo "installing NDK $NDK_VERSION (attempt $attempt/3)"
+          rm -rf "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION"
+          if "$SDKMANAGER" --install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION"; then
+            echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION installed"
+            exit 0
+          fi
+          echo "::warning::sdkmanager NDK install failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
+          sleep 10
+        done
+        echo "::error::NDK $NDK_VERSION install failed after 3 attempts — gh-1655 red'd the leg on a single truncated archive; inspect the sdkmanager output above"
+        exit 1

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1656
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1656
- **Title**: gh-1655 [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1655` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +726
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-16T14:03:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T11:24:06Z

## PR Description

Closes #1655
### Root Cause

Stuttering OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7 via `aiin`) re-send stream frames; the shared adapter mishandled both shapes: `_dedupeOverlap` trimmed overlaps only for `k >= 2`, so a 1-char punctuation stutter survived (doubled punctuation in thinking), and `_ensureToolCallBlock` matched blocks only by `streamIndex`/`id`, so a re-sent call frame with a fresh id spawned a second identical block and executed the command twice.

### Fix

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`:
  - `_dedupeOverlap`: trim 1-char overlaps too, with an ellipsis guard (a delta repeating its leading char is a legit `...` continuation, not a seam); full-snapshot branch and 64-char window unchanged.
  - `_ensureToolCallBlock` + new `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: on a lookup miss, a frame whose name equals the last registered block's name with `partialArgs` empty or a prefix of the incoming args is a re-send — merge into that block (newer id adopted only if the old is empty), appending only the non-overlapping argument suffix.

### Test Coverage

- `test/providers/openai_completions_test.dart`: stutter-trim (`greeting`, `.`, `.` → `greeting. I should`), ellipsis intact (`hmm`, `.`, `..` → `hmm...`), re-sent frame with fresh id → ONE block/one execution, distinct calls → two blocks. All failed-before/green-after as specified.
- Existing sliding-window fixture updated: `'Продолжжжжаем'` → `'Продолжжжаем'` (it baked in the surviving 1-char stutter); clean-delta cases byte-identical (C4).
- Full suite: 6549 passed, 19 failed — all 19 verified pre-existing on the clean base commit (`124f1e0`) via a detached worktree run (env-dependent PTY/CLI suites already red on main per gh-1649); provider suites: 827/827 green.

### Notes

- Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction.
- AC4 (live `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7` check) is not executable in this environment; the fixtures reproduce both observed defects at the adapter level.

+name: android-ndk-preinstall
+description: >-
+  Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK so Gradle configuration never
+  triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download mid-build. gh-1655: one
+  truncated android-ndk-r28c-linux download ("Error on ZipFile unknown
+  archive" at 33%) red'd the ci.yml build-android leg — and the aggregate
+  Quality gate with it — because AGP's in-configuration auto-install path
+  has NO retry. The NDK version is resolved from the pinned Flutter SDK's
+  own gradle plugin source (the exact value flutter.ndkVersion resolves
+  to — no second pin to drift), the install is skipped when the NDK is
+  already present, and the download itself is bounded-retried — the same
+  hardening the flutter_gemma Android seed carries (gh-1468). Companion
+  guard: test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart.
+runs:
+  using: composite
+  steps:
+    - name: Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK (bounded retry)
+      shell: bash
+      run: |
+        set -euo pipefail
+        # flutter.ndkVersion's single source of truth: the gradle plugin
+        # bundled with the SDK flutter-action installed. app/
+        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so
+        # resolving here can never skew from what AGP requests at
+        # configuration time (a literal pin on either side would break
+        # that coupling — the guard test pins both sides).
+        if [ -n "${FLUTTER_ROOT:-}" ]; then
+          FLUTTER_HOME="$FLUTTER_ROOT"
+        else
+          FLUTTER_BIN="$(command -v flutter || true)"
+          if [ -z "$FLUTTER_BIN" ]; then
+            echo "::error::cannot locate flutter (set FLUTTER_ROOT) — the NDK pre-install resolves the version from the SDK's gradle plugin source"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          FLUTTER_HOME="$(dirname "$(dirname "$FLUTTER_BIN")")"
+        fi
+        GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_HOME/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"
+        NDK_VERSION="$(grep -hoE 'val ndkVersion: String = "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"' "$GRADLE_SRC" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)"
+        if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
+          echo "::error::cannot resolve flutter.ndkVersion from $GRADLE_SRC — the Flutter gradle plugin layout moved; update the extraction in .github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall (and test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart) TOGETHER"
+          exit 1
+        fi
+        echo "resolved flutter.ndkVersion = $NDK_VERSION"
+        ANDROID_SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-/usr/local/lib/android/sdk}"
+        SDKMANAGER="$ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
+        if [ ! -x "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
+          SDKMANAGER="$(command -v sdkmanager || true)"
+        fi
+        if [ -z "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
+          echo "::error::sdkmanager not found (expected $ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager) — the NDK pre-install needs the Android cmdline-tools"
+          exit 1
+        fi
+        # Idempotence: AGP resolves `ndkVersion` against
+        # $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/<version> — source.properties present means
+        # the NDK is fully installed; skip the download entirely.
+        if [ -f "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties" ]; then
+          echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION already installed — skipping pre-install"
+          exit 0
+        fi
+        # Accept any license the image has not pre-accepted so the
+        # installs below never prompt (|| true: `yes` dies of SIGPIPE by
+        # design once sdkmanager stops reading).
+        yes | "$SDKMANAGER" --licenses > /dev/null || true
+        # gh-1655: Gradle's own auto-install (the same sdkmanager call,
+        # run inside configuration) has no retry — one truncated download
+        # unzips as "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" and the build dies.
+        # Here the same download gets three attempts with backoff.
+        for attempt in 1 2 3; do
+          echo "installing NDK $NDK_VERSION (attempt $attempt/3)"
+          rm -rf "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION"
+          if "$SDKMANAGER" --install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION"; then
+            echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION installed"
+            exit 0
+          fi
+          echo "::warning::sdkmanager NDK install failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
+          sleep 10
+        done
+        echo "::error::NDK $NDK_VERSION install failed after 3 attempts — gh-1655 red'd the leg on a single truncated archive; inspect the sdkmanager output above"
+        exit 1

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1656
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1656
- **Title**: gh-1655 [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1655` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +726
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-16T14:03:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T11:24:06Z

## PR Description

Closes #1655
### Root Cause

Stuttering OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7 via `aiin`) re-send stream frames; the shared adapter mishandled both shapes: `_dedupeOverlap` trimmed overlaps only for `k >= 2`, so a 1-char punctuation stutter survived (doubled punctuation in thinking), and `_ensureToolCallBlock` matched blocks only by `streamIndex`/`id`, so a re-sent call frame with a fresh id spawned a second identical block and executed the command twice.

### Fix

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`:
  - `_dedupeOverlap`: trim 1-char overlaps too, with an ellipsis guard (a delta repeating its leading char is a legit `...` continuation, not a seam); full-snapshot branch and 64-char window unchanged.
  - `_ensureToolCallBlock` + new `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: on a lookup miss, a frame whose name equals the last registered block's name with `partialArgs` empty or a prefix of the incoming args is a re-send — merge into that block (newer id adopted only if the old is empty), appending only the non-overlapping argument suffix.

### Test Coverage

- `test/providers/openai_completions_test.dart`: stutter-trim (`greeting`, `.`, `.` → `greeting. I should`), ellipsis intact (`hmm`, `.`, `..` → `hmm...`), re-sent frame with fresh id → ONE block/one execution, distinct calls → two blocks. All failed-before/green-after as specified.
- Existing sliding-window fixture updated: `'Продолжжжжаем'` → `'Продолжжжаем'` (it baked in the surviving 1-char stutter); clean-delta cases byte-identical (C4).
- Full suite: 6549 passed, 19 failed — all 19 verified pre-existing on the clean base commit (`124f1e0`) via a detached worktree run (env-dependent PTY/CLI suites already red on main per gh-1649); provider suites: 827/827 green.

### Notes

- Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction.
- AC4 (live `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7` check) is not executable in this environment; the fixtures reproduce both observed defects at the adapter level.

This is a real (probabilistic) regression for clean relays in thinking text. The old k>=2 floor had the same class of bug but at 2-char coincidence; k=1 makes single-char coincidences at word boundaries trigger it. I'll classify as IMPORTANT (not blocking: works as shipped for the reported defect, corrupts thinking only in a heuristic edge — but the PR description explicitly claims "clean-delta cases byte-identical (C4)" which only covered `['let me ', 'think']`).

Proposed fix: restrict the 1-char trim to the actual observed stutter shape — the re-sent standalone token. Options:
- Only trim k=1 when the overlap char is a non-letter (punctuation/whitespace), since the observed stutter is punctuation doubling and prose rarely starts a fresh delta with the same punctuation as the tail.
- Or only when delta is a single char AND equal to text's last char AND... hmm "greeting." + "." delta length 1 → trim. The "yes"+"sir" case has delta length>1 starting with same char.
- Narrowest: trim 1-char only when the whole delta is exactly that one repeated char (delta.length == 1) or when the char is non-alphanumeric.

Actually let me reconsider severity. BLOCKING = "broken behavior, failing gates, scope violations, security". This is a correctness regression risk on clean relays for thinking text only (cosmetic display text, not executed commands). The tool-call merge affects executed commands and it's guarded reasonably. I'd call the dedupe issue IMPORTANT (should fix before merge) — some might argue BLOCKING since it's a behavior regression on a code path that worked before for clean relays. Hmm. The k>=2 version already corrupted in rarer cases, so this is an amplification of a known trade-off. IMPORTANT seems right, with a concrete suggested narrowing. If the machine protocol maps any BLOCKING → REQUEST_CHANGES, IMPORTANT findings allow APPROVE. Let me think about whether anything is truly BLOCKING:

- CI status: no ci_failures.md input. The discussion history shows repeated red heads, but the latest commits (guard crash fix 065579, merge c0b2f79) came after the last recorded red at 06:08Z. Guard test review:

Adapter: one more check — `_matchResentToolCallBlock` iterates `blocks.reversed` to find last ToolCallStreamingBlock. If the last tool-call block belongs to the PREVIOUS message... within one stream/session, blocks accumulate across messages? `_OpenAICompletionsSession` — per stream presumably; tool calls all in one assistant message. OK.

Edge: frame with `index` present and matching an existing block, but ALSO name matching last block with prefix args — resend computed FIRST (before lookup) and takes precedence: `block = resent ?? _lookupToolCallBlock(...)`. So if a frame arrives with an index that maps to block A, but the name/args ALSO match the last block B (different), we'd merge into B while the index says A! Wait — can that happen? `_matchResentToolCallBlock` checks only name+args prefix, NOT id/index. Scenario: streamIndex=0 maps to block A (first call), the frame's name = 'bash', args = prefix of... `_matchResentToolCallBlock` checks against the LAST block (B, second call). If B's args empty or prefix of incoming args and names equal — resend=B, and the frame intended for A (by index) merges into B! That misroutes a frame. Concrete: call A `bash` args complete `{"command":"ls"}`; call B `bash` just started, name set, args empty. Frame arrives: {index: 0, function: {arguments: 'more for A'?}}. Hmm — but frames carry only arguments fragments, not name usually in later chunks. `_matchResentToolCallBlock` requires `function['name']` non-empty — later chunks don't carry name, so match requires name present. Frames carrying name are typically initial frames. If an initial frame for B carries {index:1, id:new, name:'bash', args:'{"command":"pwd"}'} while A exists with args `{"command":"ls"}`: match checks B (last block, args empty) → prefix condition (existing empty → matches) → resend=B. But what if the frame carries index:0 mapping to A with name 'bash'? A lookup would hit A by index — but resend short-circuits. Frame {index: 0, name: 'bash', args: '...'} — index 0 maps to A; last block is B with name 'bash' and empty args → resend=B → frame merges into B, A never gets it. Is a relay sending index:0 name-bearing frames mid-stream realistic? In OpenAI streaming, only the FIRST chunk of each call carries index+id+name; subsequent chunks carry index+args. A stutter re-send of the first chunk carries the same index (0 for first call). Hmm — for the FIRST call's stutter, last block == A (only block) → fine. The misroute needs ≥2 blocks and a name-bearing frame whose index maps to an EARLIER block while the LAST block has same name + empty/prefix args. E.g. relay re-sends call A's first frame {index:0, id:fresh, name:'bash', args:'{"command":"ls"}'} AFTER call B began (B: name 'bash', args empty). Then resend=B, args `{"command":"ls"}` merge into B → B executes `ls`, A keeps its own args → both A and B execute the same command? A already has `{"command":"ls"}` → A executes ls, B now also ls → DOUBLE EXECUTION — the exact bug this PR fixes, resurrected in a two-call interleaved stutter. But wait — `_matchResentToolCallBlock` doesn't check streamIndex at all. If the frame has index 0 and toolCallBlocksByIndex[0] exists, that's a strong signal it's NOT a fresh-id resend (real re-sends per the bug have fresh ids but same index... hmm, actually the bug's re-send had no index at all in the fixture — both frames lack `index`).

This is getting deep. Realistically: stutter re-sends duplicate a frame; if the duplicate carries the same index, the index lookup HITS (index registered) and no duplicate occurs even without this PR. The PR's fixture frames have no index field. A relay that re-sends with a fresh id would normally keep the same index — in which case index lookup saves us. The fresh-id-no-index shape is the one fixed. The misroute scenario requires the re-sent frame to arrive after a second same-name call started AND carry a name AND carry an index pointing at the first call AND fresh id — quite contrived, and even then: merging into B with A-intended args... Actually wait, if the frame carries index:0, `_matchResentToolCallBlock` should arguably bail when `streamIndex` resolves to an existing block. That's a clean hardening: in `_matchResentToolCallBlock`, return null if `toolCall['index']` is an int that maps to an existing block in `toolCallBlocksByIndex` (that lookup will succeed in `_ensureToolCallBlock`). This closes the misroute. SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT.

I'll fold this into one IMPORTANT comment on `_matchResentToolCallBlock` with both sub-points (index precedence + partial/overlap resend not covered + new id not registered for reasoning-details). Hmm, keep comments focused. Let me structure findings:
